memory_candidates.content: In this environment, `grep` is invocation-context-dependent, not a single fact: a raw command typed or pasted directly into an agent's own Bash-tool shell resolves `grep` to a non-exported interactive shell function that execs the Claude Code binary with ARGV0=ugrep (real ugrep 7.8.4 semantics), while the identical command placed inside a `.sh` file executed as a subprocess (`bash file.sh`, `./file.sh`, or a hook-runner spawn) resolves plain `grep` to GNU grep 3.12, because the function is not exported and $BASH_ENV is empty. Verify which context applies (env -i bash -lc 'grep --version' vs. the top-level Bash-tool shell) before assuming either engine when auditing or writing grep-based patterns.

ugrep 7.8.4's -E (POSIX/DFA) engine mis-evaluates \b compositionally: a \b downstream of an earlier \b-anchored subexpression separated by a wildcard run (e.g. [^|]*) can silently NOMATCH even though every individual fragment matches in isolation and -P (PCRE2) on the same unmodified pattern matches correctly. A single \b, or one \b...\b bracket around a single alternation/token (shape \bWORD\b or \b(A|B|C)\s+N\b), is not affected -- only a chain of 2+ independent \b-anchored subexpressions in one linear pattern is at risk. Always test the full, unmodified production pattern against a real positive AND negative input under the actual deployed engine before trusting a \b-bearing pattern; never generalize from a simplified stand-in.
